content.diagnostic_criteria: Wall thickness >14 mm in one or more LV myocardial segments not explained solely by abnormal loading conditions. LVOTO ≥30 mmHg at rest or exercise, asymmetric hypertrophy, or increased LGE in a patchy mid-wall pattern in the most hypertrophied segment suggest HCM. Consider familial HCM when two or more first- or second-degree relatives with HCM or a first-degree relative with autopsy-proven HCM and sudden death at <50 years are detected.
content.differential_diagnosis: Distinguish genetic HCM from physiological hypertrophy (athletes), severe hypertension, aortic stenosis, isolated septal hypertrophy; consider amyloidosis when there is increased thickness of the interatrial septum, AV valve and/or RV free wall.
content.genetic_counselling_and_testing: Genetic testing should be offered to all patients with HCM to identify a possible underlying genetic cause and to first-degree adult relatives of patients with a definite disease-causing mutation. Clinical evaluation, ECG and echocardiography should be performed in first-degree relatives. If no definite mutation is identified or testing is not performed, repeat clinical evaluation every 2–5 years or less if non-diagnostic abnormalities are present.
content.minimal_set_of_genes: Minimal set of genes (sarcomeric gene mutation in up to 60% of cases) listed: TTN, LMNA, MHC, TNNT, Troponin-C, MYPC, RMB20, PLN, Sodium channel alpha unit, BAG3, Actin Alpha Cardiac Muscle, Nexilin, Tropomyosin-1, Vinculin.
content.sequencing_recommendation: Consider additional sequencing of a very large panel of genes when there is a clear familial history or structural phenotype, preferably combined with family segregation.
content.specific_conditions: Muscular weakness: consider mitochondrial X-linked mutations, glycogen storage disorders, FHLI mutations, Friedreich ataxia. Syndromic conditions (cognitive, visual impairment, drooping eyelid): consider mitochondrial X-linked mutations, Noonan syndrome, Danon disease. Café au lait spots (lentigines): consider Leopard/Noonan syndrome.
